  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Parks & Recreation Director
Date:  March 6, 2025
Subject:  Review of Concession Agreements

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File
Report Summary: Each year the Commission reviews the Department’s current
concession agreements and provides staff with recommendations, particularly for those
agreements that are currently up for extension or renewal. Typically, agreements are
those that allow a private business, either for profit or non-profit, to conduct business on
Park property or to operate a program on behalf of the City.
On the following page is a list of the concession agreements that are currently active
along with information regarding their expiration dates.

We are working with both our carnival operator and our Vet Care operator to either
extend their current contracts or go out to bid for a new vendor. Customarily, we do not
get bids from other carnival contractors as they tend to have an agreement amongst
themselves not to bid for areas already taken by the current company. In the case of
the Vet Care operator, staff will be working with them to see if we can get an extension
of services as they are one of the few in the area who offer vaccinations on a monthly
basis.

Overall, we are happy with the current providers and are not recommending any major
changes at this time.

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  April 10, 2025
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 3
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Tina Fierro, Deputy Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  March 6, 2025
Subject:  Review of Parks & Recreation Revenues

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File
Report Summary: Commissioner Pelayo requested this item; to discuss revenue
generating events.

The Parks & Recreation Department is a “General Fund” department in the City of
South Gate that provides essential services to the residents of South Gate. While the
department brings in over $2 million in funds each year through rental of facilities and
program fees. The expenses to operate these facilities and programs far exceed the
revenue brought in each year. Each new program, activity, or special event usually
costs the City significantly more than the monies that are brought in to support the
event.

South Gate has always prioritized the need for Parks & Recreation and understands
that these costs are part of what makes the City a desirable place to live and raise
families. The Department does want to do it’s part in keeping costs down by making
appropriate cost increases on a yearly basis, as well as, looking for event sponsors to
help us with our programming needs, but these measures are not enough to keep us
out of the red.

In past years, the Department in conjunction with Community Development has looked
into Quimby Fees (requiring developers to pay fees for dedicated park space) to help
with the overall costs, but due to Covid and other issues these were never acted upon.

As far as overall revenue generating events, the carnival operation at the Azalea
Festival and 4th of July are about the only two that provide more income than expenses.
We have had talks with producers about large concerts using the park that could
provide significant funding, but the promoter we were working with fell ill and wasn’t able
to continue.

Overall, the Parks & Recreation Department is dependent on the General Fund to
operate the day-to-day activities. We do really well at getting grants for the larger
  Page 1 of 2

  6
 infrastructure needs, but these funds do not usually take care of the maintenance and
programming costs. If there are revenue generating events that would help our bottom
line, the staff would be happy to look into them for the coming fiscal year.

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  April 10, 2025
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 4
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Jose Covarrubias, Facility Maintenance Supervisor
Date:  March 27, 2025

Subject:  Park Facility Maintenance Division Annual Report

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:
The following is a report on what this Division has performed and accomplished during
the past year.

The Park Facilities Division has successfully hosted, organized, and facilitated a wide
array of events throughout the year. This includes both recurring City sponsored events,
such as Winter Wonderland, Azalea Festival, LA Philharmonic performance, and
community focused events like facility and picnic reservations, sports activities, food
giveaways, blood drives, job fairs, and various educational classes. Our team has
demonstrated adaptability and efficiency in supporting these events, ensuring their
smooth execution from setup to teardown.

To enhance our operational capabilities, we invested in new disinfecting equipment,
including portable disinfectant sprayers, floor auto-scrubbing machines, and portable
pressure washers. These additions have significantly improved our ability to maintain
cleanliness and hygiene across both indoor and outdoor park facilities, ensuring the
safety and comfort of all park users.

We welcomed a new Park Facility Maintenance Worker to the team. This new position
has been crucial in covering weekend shifts, enhancing our ability to maintain park
facilities consistently throughout the week.

Additionally, we installed privacy walls at two of our parks, State Street and Cesar
Chavez, both along Southern Avenue. This improvement allows us to leave restroom
doors in the open position, addressing safety concerns, and preventing users from
inadvertently locking themselves in restrooms for extended periods.

The Community Service Worker Program has been instrumental in supporting the Park
Facilities Division. Currently, the program is accepting up to fifteen volunteers to assist

  Page 1 of 2
  8
 with Facility Maintenance and Grounds staff, with the potential to expand the number of
volunteers as needed. This program has provided valuable support, contributing to the
overall efficiency and upkeep of our facilities.

To accommodate the growing number of classes, reservations, and events, staff
schedules have been adjusted to ensure full coverage and support. Facility staff has
displayed exceptional flexibility and professionalism in managing the transition between
regular operations and new demands, consistently responding to the evolving needs of
the Division.

The Park Facilities Division has made significant strides in improving the quality and
efficiency of its operations over the past year. With the support of dedicated staff, new
equipment, and the continued engagement of community volunteers, we are well-
positioned to continue delivering quality services and maintaining the City's parks and
facilities.

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  April 10, 2025
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 5
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  March 6, 2025
Subject:  Proposed Program Fees for 2025/26

Recommended Motion:  Approve the Proposed Program Fee Schedule for May 11,
2025, to May 11, 2026.

Report Summary: On a regular basis, the Parks & Recreation Department reviews the
fees they charge for different programs offered by the Department so that they can be
brought in-line with the costs to provide the programs. Annually, we bring to the
Commission a report on the fees and any proposed changes that are being
recommended for the upcoming fiscal year.

Last year the Parks & Recreation Department raised rates for programs/classes by
3.5% due to the inflation from the past year. The only exception to the price increase
was the Adult Sports Programs which had seen drops in registration in the previous
years and staff felt it would be best to leave pricing the same to encourage additional
signups in this program.

The Cost Of Living Annually in the Los Angeles/Long Beach area rose last year by 3.4%
and Minimum Wage in California increased from $16.00 hr. to $16.50 hr. in January of
this year. Usually, staff would recommend that we cover the cost of inflation with
updated rates for our programs, but this year, the City of South Gate is implementing a
“Convenience” fee for all credit card transactions in the amount of 3.5% across the
board. Staff feel that the fee is significant enough to warrant leaving our current pricing
system in place for this year as we don’t want to push pricing so high that we start to
lose participants. Please note that a large majority of our patrons use their credit cards
to pay for programs/memberships/rentals so this in a sense will be a 3.5% price
increase for all our users.

In addition, this change for Sports Center memberships will require us to start fresh with
all of our memberships affecting 3,000+ patrons and staff feels it would be detrimental
to add additional price hikes to this process at this time.

Attached is the Fee Schedule showing current fees. Staff will be on hand to answer
questions.
